{{nihongo|'''Sigekatu Kuroda'''|黒田 成勝|Kuroda Shigekatsu|extra= 11 November 1905 – 3 November 1972}} was a Japanese [[mathematician]] who worked in [[number theory]] and [[mathematical logic]].<ref name=MacTutor>{{MacTutor Biography|id=Kuroda}}</ref>

In 1942 he became a professor at the newly founded [[Nagoya University#History|Nagoya Imperial University]], where he stayed for over twenty years. He was responsible for much of the effort in setting up its Department of Mathematics.<ref>{{cite journal| author = H. W. Leopoldt | author-link=Heinrich-Wolfgang Leopoldt | title = Obituary : Sigekatu Kuroda (November 11, 1905–November 3, 1972) | journal= [[J. Number Theory]] | volume=7 |year= 1975|pages= 1–4| doi=10.1016/0022-314X(75)90002-5 |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82788217.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225082804/https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82788217.pdf|archive-date=2025-02-25| doi-access= free }}</ref>

He was married to the renowned number theorist [[Teiji Takagi]]'s daughter Yakeo. The couple had three sons, all of whom became mathematicians, including [[S.-Y. Kuroda]], who was a professor of [[linguistics]] at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ling.ucsd.edu/kuroda/obituary.html|title=Obituary for S.-Y. Kuroda, UCSD Linguistics Department}}</ref>

He published a text on the foundations of [[algebraic number theory]] with [[Tomio Kubota]] in 1963.
